tasks.goal: In semver_range.py, satisfies(version, rng) decides whether a semantic version satisfies an npm-style range. Versions are MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with an optional -PRERELEASE of dot-separated identifiers; anything else raises ValueError. Precedence: compare MAJOR, MINOR, PATCH numerically; a version with a prerelease is lower than the same version without one; prerelease identifiers compare left to right, numeric ones numerically, alphanumeric ones lexically, numeric lower than alphanumeric, and a shorter list is lower when all shared identifiers are equal. A range is one or more comparator sets joined by '||' (satisfied if any set is); a set is space-separated comparators that must all hold: =V, V, >V, >=V, <V, <=V. '^V' means >=V and below the next major when MAJOR > 0, below 0.(MINOR+1).0 when MAJOR is 0 and MINOR > 0, and below 0.0.(PATCH+1) when both are 0. '~V' means >=V and below MAJOR.(MINOR+1).0. X-ranges: '*' or '' match any version; '1.x', '1.X', '1.*' and '1' mean >=1.0.0 <2.0.0; '1.2.x' and '1.2' mean >=1.2.0 <1.3.0. Hyphen ranges 'A - B' mean >=A and <=B, where a partial B such as '1.4' means below 1.5.0. A version with a prerelease satisfies a set only if some comparator in that set carries a prerelease on the same MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH; otherwise prerelease versions never match. An unparsable range raises ValueError.

import pytest

import semver_range


def test_sv5ao01_compositional():
    s = semver_range.satisfies
    assert s('1.2.3', '^1.0.0') and not s('2.0.0', '^1.0.0')
    assert s('0.2.5', '^0.2.3') and not s('0.3.0', '^0.2.3') and not s('0.0.4', '^0.0.3')
    assert s('1.2.9', '~1.2.3') and not s('1.3.0', '~1.2.3')
    assert s('1.4.9', '1.2.3 - 1.4') and not s('1.5.0', '1.2.3 - 1.4')

tasks.goal: In intervals.py, merge(intervals) flattens labelled half-open intervals [start, end) that may overlap into non-overlapping segments. Each input is (start, end, label, priority) with int start < end (anything else raises ValueError). Every point covered by at least one interval belongs to the interval with the highest priority there; on equal priority the one that comes first in the input wins. Return (start, end, label) segments sorted by start; uncovered gaps produce no segment; adjacent segments with the same label are joined into one.
